rv.q: The occasions of character veracity aside, El Guindi’s play is sharp and engaging, and contains promise.
People of the Book is, without a doubt, a true masterpiece.
Neither the script nor the program for People of the Book states when the play takes place, so presumably it is the present.

cn.t: Critics split on this morally complex drama about war and truth, with some praising its exploration of flawed humanity while others find the script confused and its treatment of the Iraq insurgency outdated.
